provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Ext family batch, book archetype. Small residential tickets; the value is recurring plans and storefront routes, so products stay cheap and route-shaped. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Window count by size, storeys, inside and outside, French panes, skylights, sunrooms and hard-to-reach glass, with a price range before booking
pageStructurePlus.why: Window cleaning is priced by panes, not hours. A homeowner who can count their windows can book tonight without a visit.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Screen washing and repair, track vacuuming, sill wiping, sprinkler hard-water stains, and sticker or paint removal after construction
pageStructurePlus.why: Add-ons are where the margin is. Listing them clearly turns a basic outside-only clean into a full visit.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Spring and fall, quarterly or monthly plans, inside-out alternation, route days by neighbourhood, and plan sign-up with card on file
pageStructurePlus.why: One-off cleans pay the bills; plans build the business. A plan page makes 'see you in the fall' an automatic booking.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Weekly or monthly storefront glass, door glass and signage, before-opening service times, monthly invoicing, and a route sign-up for shop owners
pageStructurePlus.why: Storefront routes are steady, small and recurring. Shop owners want to know the day, the time and the monthly price.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Pure-water poles for second-storey glass, ladder standoffs that protect gutters, insurance, protecting landscaping, and what happens on a rainy day
pageStructurePlus.why: Homeowners worry about ladders on their gutters and someone falling. Explaining the method and insurance settles it.

designDirections.name: Sparkle Day

designDirections.headlineSample: Window cleaning in {City}, inside and out
designDirections.whyItFits: Sky blue and soft rounded type feel friendly and light, like clean glass. The page is a pane-count quote and a Book button.

designDirections.name: Clear Every Season
designDirections.bestFor: Window cleaning companies selling recurring residential plans and add-ons with online booking
designDirections.headlineSample: Streak-free windows on a schedule across {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: The family's own combo. Evergreen and a refined serif read like a dependable service you let into your house, and the card stack shows plans side by side.

designDirections.name: Estate Glass
designDirections.bestFor: Window cleaners serving large homes with many panes, skylights, chandeliers and discreet scheduling

openers.line: Your Maps listing has reviews about spotless glass but nowhere to book. People decide they're sick of streaky windows on a sunny afternoon and want a cleaning date right then.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there's no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: A window cleaning booking page for that button: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing points to Facebook. Someone wanting their windows cleaned before guests arrive needs a price by pane count and a date, not a feed to scroll.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link and confirm it's Facebook. Note the most recent window job posted.
openers.linkLine: A window cleaning page with prices and booking: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your window cleaning site still has a free-host banner and a contact form that bounces. For a business that sells clear glass, it looks a little foggy.
openers.hook: Open the site and look for a banner, a stale copyright or a broken form. Note which.
openers.linkLine: The same window cleaner, a clear page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your window cleaning prices sit in a table that I had to pinch and zoom on my phone. Most people book a window washer from their phone.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your window cleaning site rebuilt for phones: {demo-link}

openers.line: Right now, finding out what you charge for windows means messaging you. A quick count of panes and storeys gives a price and books the window cleaning in one go.
openers.hook: Check their profile, listing and any site for prices. If there are none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A pane-count quote that books itself: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your squeegee clips are the kind people watch twice. Right now they end with nowhere to book a window cleaning, just a comment section.
openers.hook: Find a short squeegee or water-fed pole clip on their profile. Note what it shows.
openers.linkLine: Those squeegee clips with a Book button below: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews mention shoe covers and towels under every sill. Letting someone in to clean inside windows takes trust, and those reviews are the trust. They just never leave Google.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about care inside the house. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Those window cleaning reviews where people book: {demo-link}

openers.line: Spring is when everyone notices winter grime on the glass and window cleaning calendars fill in days. Online booking means you're full before your competitors call back.
openers.hook: Use in late winter or early spring. Name the season in the reply.

openers.line: Before the holidays, people want their windows clean for guests and book at night after work. If booking a window cleaner means a daytime call, the date goes to someone else.
openers.hook: Use in October and November. Check whether any online booking exists.
openers.linkLine: Holiday window cleaning, bookable at night: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring another window cleaner. A plan page that keeps the calendar full is what pays a second person through the slow months.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A window cleaning page with plans and careers: {demo-link}

openers.line: You clean storefront windows as well as homes. Shop owners want a weekly or monthly window route price and a set day, and there's no page for them to sign up.
openers.hook: Only if they've posted storefront or commercial glass. Note the shop type.

openers.line: If customers already book you every spring and fall, a window cleaning plan sign-up makes that automatic and fills your routes months ahead.
openers.hook: Look for reviews like 'they come every season'. Quote it back.

openers.line: Second-storey window cleaning means ladders against someone's house. A page showing your insurance and your pole method settles the nervous homeowner.
openers.hook: Check whether they mention insurance or water-fed poles. Never quote a policy you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Insurance and methods on one window cleaning page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Neighbours keep tagging you whenever someone wants a window cleaner recommended. The people who follow that tag can't pick a date or see a price anywhere.
openers.hook: Search a neighbourhood or HOA group for their name. Note one thread.
openers.linkLine: Where those window cleaning recommendations could book: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted shows windows so clear they look open. It deserves to be the first thing people see on a window cleaning page, right above the Book button.
openers.hook: Pick their newest job post and name it: house style, sunroom, storefront, and the street if tagged.
openers.linkLine: That window cleaning job, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted is crystal clear glass, lovely work.

I looked for window cleaners in {City} and found {Business Name}, but no way to get a price by window count or book a date without messaging. I mocked up a sample booking site to see how it would look, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Shall I send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, nudging this up in case it got lost. Here's the sample window cleaning site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a pane-count quote, online booking, screen and track add-ons, a recurring plan sign-up and a storefront route page. If it's not for you, tell me and I'll leave it there.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build booking sites for window cleaners in {City}. I sent a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"No problem. Quick version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} where customers count their windows, see a price and book, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I text you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think of it?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range} depending on plans and storefront pages, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and price changes. For a window cleaner your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, which a handful of plan customers covers."
"Could I show you around it for ten minutes one evening this week?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a short scope and a deposit invoice. It's live before spring cleaning season."

objections.objection: My customers just text me when they want a clean.
objections.handler: "That works for the ones you have. New people won't text a stranger, they'll book whoever shows a price. And a plan means your regulars don't have to remember to text."

objections.objection: Window cleaning jobs are too small for a website.
objections.handler: "Each one is. A route of plan customers isn't. The site is there to sign up plans and storefronts, not single cleans."

objections.objection: I can't price without seeing the house.
objections.handler: "It gives a range by pane count and storeys, and you confirm on arrival. Most people only need a ballpark to book."

objections.objection: Winter is slow and money's tight.
objections.handler: "That's why winter is when to build it. The plan sign-ups fill your spring before the first warm day."

objections.objection: I'm fine with word of mouth.
objections.handler: "Word of mouth sends people to search your name. Right now they find a listing with no way to book. The site catches the referral."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, for the pane-count quote, booking and a plan page. A few plan customers pay it back."

email.subject: Booking site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build booking sites for window cleaners in {City} and made a sample for {Business Name} with a pane-count quote. I'll text the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm tidying up demos on Friday and the {Business Name} window cleaning one is on the list.

Want me to keep it? Just a yes or no.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, spring window cleaning season is close and calendars fill fast once the sun shows the winter grime. Thought of you.

The booking site's still here, same price. {demo-link} if you'd like another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a handful of plan customers, never to a big-ticket build; single cleans are small.
Price the pane-count quote as its own line; it replaces the back-and-forth over text.
Plans with card on file are the most valuable piece; price the sign-up separately.
Only add a storefront route page for cleaners who already do commercial glass.
Keep add-on pages small: screens, tracks and hard water belong on one page, not three.
Products for this trade should pay back within one season; keep monthly prices low.

lineItems.item: Pane-count quote with storeys and add-ons
lineItems.description: Max when it covers French panes, skylights, screens, tracks and hard water with inside-out options.

lineItems.item: Recurring plan sign-up with card on file
lineItems.description: Max with several plan frequencies, route-day selection and automatic rebooking.
Max with weekly or monthly options, before-opening times and monthly invoicing set up.
Max with before-and-after sliders and a post-construction cleaning request form.
Max when each page shows that neighbourhood's route day and local jobs.
Max when the quote, plan sign-up and storefront page are all translated.

whatElseYouSell.name: Squeegee clip filming morning
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A morning filming squeegee passes, water-fed pole rinses and sparkling sunrooms gives you a month of short window cleaning clips."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, on a bright day with a big glass job booked.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile posts of window cleaning jobs
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Each week a sunroom, storefront or second-storey window cleaning job goes on your Google profile with the neighbourhood, so the map shows you're out every day."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the site is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests after each window clean
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "When the sun hits the clean glass that afternoon, the customer gets a text asking how the window cleaner did. That's when they notice."

whatElseYouSell.name: Van magnet and door hanger design
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A neat van magnet and a door hanger with a neighbour discount turn each window cleaning visit into the next house on the street."

whatElseYouSell.name: Same-street door hangers on route days
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "On a route day, the houses either side get a hanger saying their window cleaner is already on the street next month, with a booking code."

whatElseYouSell.name: Spring and holiday cleaning pushes
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Two short pushes a year, spring grime and holiday guests, to past customers and local groups fill the window cleaning calendar at its two peaks."

whatElseYouSell.name: Storefront route flyer for shop owners
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A one-page flyer with your weekly storefront window price, walked into every shop on the block, turns one commercial stop into a route."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, for cleaners with any storefront work.

withoutAI.route: Pressure washers on the same houses
withoutAI.pitchLine: "House wash and window cleaning go together on every spring list. The washer you swap customers with needs a booking site too."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Same houses, same season, no overlap in service.

withoutAI.route: House cleaners who skip outside glass
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Maid services get asked about windows constantly and send it to you. They need a booking site as much as any window cleaner."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Residential cleaners are a large, referral-friendly trade that buys booking sites.

withoutAI.route: Gutter cleaners on the ladder route
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Gutter cleaning and window cleaning happen the same spring and fall weeks. Your gutter partner needs a plan sign-up page."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Overlapping seasons and customers; both sell plans.

withoutAI.route: Shop owners on the storefront route
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The shops whose windows you clean weekly have their own website problems, and they already trust you with their front door."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Small retailers need sites and see you every week.

withoutAI.route: Builders who need post-construction glass cleaning
withoutAI.whoPays: The home builder, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Every new build needs stickers and paint scraped off the glass before closing. The builder who calls your window cleaner needs a better site."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Small builders are under-served online and refer final-clean trades.

withoutAI.route: Realtors and stagers before listing photos
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Agents book window cleaning before listing photos. They need a vendor page, and your client is the window cleaner on it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Agents buy credibility and send steady pre-listing work.

withAI.pitchLine: "The maid service you trade window referrals with gets a bot that quotes by bedrooms and bathrooms and offers your window cleaning as an add-on."
withAI.whyItWorks: Configuration of a quote flow you know, with your client built in.

withAI.pitchLine: "A small assistant that reminds a shop owner when the windows, mats, pest visit and hood cleaning are due, and books the window route day."
withAI.whyItWorks: Owners forget recurring vendors; the window cleaner gets a sticky slot.

withAI.pitchLine: "Agents upload a walkthrough and get a prep checklist, windows, wash, touch-up, with the local vendors to book."
withAI.whyItWorks: Agents want quick seller prep; the window cleaner is first on the list.

withAI.pitchLine: "Builders get an assistant that turns walkthrough notes into a closing punch list and books the final window cleaning automatically."
withAI.whyItWorks: Builders need clean closings; the window client gets every final clean.

withAI.pitchLine: "Your washing partner gets a tool that quotes driveways and siding from a house shot, with window cleaning offered after."
"The gutter cleaner you share houses with gets automated spring and fall reminders that offer your window cleaning in the same text."
withAI.whyItWorks: Shared seasonal timing makes joint reminders natural.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text with the pane-count quote
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Squeegee in one hand, pole in the other? Callers you can't answer get a text linking the window count quote, and most book before you're off the ladder."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their number forwarded and the quote page live.

softwareAI.name: Route-day reminders for window customers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Two days before their window cleaning, customers get a text to unlock the side gate and clear the sills, so nobody waits on the porch."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their route days and gate notes.

softwareAI.name: Plan billing for recurring window cleans
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Plan customers are charged after each window cleaning visit is marked done and rebooked for the next season automatically."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, once plans are selling. Needs plan prices and a payment account.

softwareAI.name: Storefront monthly invoicing
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every storefront on the window route gets one tidy invoice at month end listing each visit, paid by card link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, once there are several storefront accounts.

softwareAI.name: Window count from a house shot
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A homeowner uploads front and back shots and it drafts a pane count by storey, so the window cleaning quote is close before anyone counts."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs a set of past jobs with counts. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer; you confirm on arrival.

softwareAI.name: Thank-you notes for glass reviews
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When someone praises how clear their sunroom looks, a warm reply mentioning the windows and their neighbourhood is ready for your OK."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, with review requests. Needs a few past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Window route planner by neighbourhood
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Plan customers are grouped into route days by neighbourhood, so the window cleaner does a street in a morning instead of zigzagging."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, once there are enough plans to route.

softwareAI.name: Customer glass notes and gate codes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each customer's pane count, tricky windows, ladder spots, pets and gate codes saved, so any window cleaner on the crew can do the house."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their customer notes typed in once.

softwareAI.name: Window cleaning FAQ chatbot
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'do you do inside too' and 'what if it rains' at night, from your window cleaning policies, and drops the booking link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their policies and add-on list. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Before-and-after job report
softwareAI.pitchLine: "After each clean the customer gets a short report with shots of the worst windows before and after, and any broken screens flagged for repair."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs a logo and their checklist.

softwareAI.name: Hard-water stain assessor
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers upload sprinkler-spotted glass and it suggests whether it's a normal window clean or a hard-water restoration job, for you to confirm."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs past hard-water jobs with notes. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Plan member page for window customers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Members see their next window cleaning date, past reports and can add screens or tracks to the next visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs plan billing running.

softwareAI.name: Storefront route sheet app
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The storefront window route in order on a phone, with opening times, door codes and a tap to mark each shop done with a shot."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, once they run a storefront route.

softwareAI.name: Window cleaning post writer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A month of window cleaning posts drafted from your jobs and the season, spring grime, pollen, holiday guests, approved before posting."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs approval on every post. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Supplies and mileage tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Track squeegee rubber, pure-water resin, ladders and mileage per route, and see which window cleaning neighbourhoods actually pay."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a season of receipts.

softwareAI.name: Storefront prospect letter drafter
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Name a street of shops and it drafts a short letter for each, offering a weekly window cleaning slot on the route you already drive."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their storefront price. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer; you send every letter yourself.

softwareAI.name: Crew schedule for a second window cleaner
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a second window cleaner starts, each gets their own route list, customer notes and job reports on a phone."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, when they hire.

softwareAI.name: Screen repair quote helper
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Torn screens get snapped during the window clean, and it drafts a rescreen quote by size for the customer to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their screen prices. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Window cleaning applicant screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Window cleaner applicants say whether they're fine on ladders, can work inside homes and pass a background check, before you call."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: When they post a hiring note. Needs their must-haves. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Seasonal rebooking for lapsed window customers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A list of everyone who had windows cleaned last year but hasn't rebooked, with one-tap texts offering their usual route day."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs last year's customer list.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a pane-count quote for one window cleaner. Every window cleaning business answers 'how much for my house' by text all day."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Many small operators, one simple tool, a low monthly price.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A find-a-window-cleaner map on the pole and resin supplier's site sends homeowners to the operators who buy from them."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Suppliers want operators busy and loyal.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer members a window cleaning booking template with plans and storefront pages as a membership benefit."

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Starter site for window cleaning course graduates
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Window cleaning start-up courses turn out new operators who all need a booking site the week they finish."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Course owners want graduates to succeed and will bundle it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agencies with a window cleaner client can license my booking template with the pane-count quote built in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Small builds agencies don't want to design from scratch.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Window and exterior cleaning franchises need a booking site per territory with local route days. One template, many owners."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Franchises roll out the same build repeatedly.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Commercial glass schedule portal for property managers
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Managers with many low-rise buildings get one portal that schedules window cleaning visits and keeps proof-of-service shots."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Managers prefer one portal across buildings.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A downtown district can offer every shop a shared window cleaning route sign-up, with one local cleaner doing the whole street."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Districts fund clean storefronts and like one simple program.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Home cleaning marketplace add-on for maid services
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Maid services elsewhere can offer outside window cleaning through a partner booking widget routed to local window cleaners."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Every maid service gets asked about windows.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Spring and holiday campaign kit for other window cleaners
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The spring grime and holiday guest pushes, packaged with posts and texts, for window cleaners anywhere."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Every window cleaner has the same two peaks.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A window cleaner in a new suburb
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I keep one window cleaning business per suburb. {City} is covered, so the demo goes to the tidiest operator next door."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Suburbs each support a few window cleaners; the demo carries over.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "When a window cleaner's old page stops taking bookings, I swap in the pane-count template and they're live again before the next route day."

upsellLadder.offer: Window cleaning booking site plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The window cleaning site and care plan go on one contract, so changing a pane price is a text to me."

upsellLadder.offer: Review requests after each window clean
upsellLadder.trigger: The first window cleaning booked online is done.
upsellLadder.line: "That first online booking is a review waiting. Let's ask every window customer the same afternoon."

upsellLadder.offer: Plan billing for recurring window cleans
upsellLadder.line: "You've got window plan customers now. Let them pay and rebook on their own."

upsellLadder.trigger: They mention driving across town between window jobs.
upsellLadder.line: "Your window customers cluster in a few neighbourhoods. Let's make those route days."

upsellLadder.offer: Storefront route flyer for shop owners
upsellLadder.trigger: They land their first storefront through the site.
upsellLadder.line: "One storefront is a start. A flyer down the same block makes it a window route."

upsellLadder.trigger: The calendar shows open weeks heading into the spring or holiday peak.
upsellLadder.line: "There are gaps before the busy window season. Let's fill them from past customers first."

upsellLadder.offer: Crew schedule for a second window cleaner
upsellLadder.trigger: They hire a second window cleaner.
upsellLadder.line: "Two window cleaners need their own routes and notes. Let's set that up before the new hire starts."
